# Control levers in full

## Tool gating and verbatim outcomes

`tool_constraints` decide when tools appear in the model's tool list and when they
may run. `requires:` hides a tool until its memory condition holds. A closed gate
removes the tool from the model's schema, so it cannot call what it cannot see.
`tool_constraints` are enforced no matter who triggers the tool, the model or an
ordered-block `execute_tool:` step. Every key referenced must be declared in a
`memory.yml`.

`requires_confirmation:` with `enabled: true` on an irreversible tool pauses the
call and resumes only after the user confirms through `resolve_tool_confirmation`
(`confirmed=true` runs the stored call; `confirmed=false` cancels it). The nested
`utter_for_confirmation` and `utter_on_user_denial` optionally name responses in
`responses.yml`: the engine sends a supplied ask or denial itself, and the model
handles the ones you leave out. `requires_confirmation: { enabled: true }` turns
the gate on without engine-owned text. Calling the gated tool again while the
confirmation is pending returns an error.

`on_success:` / `on_failure:` name verbatim responses sent after the tool result
(success or error payload).

```yaml
tool_constraints:
  - lock_card:
      requires: "session.card_replace.selected_card_id"
  - process_card_replacement:
      requires: "session.card_replace.shipping_type"
      requires_confirmation:
        enabled: true
        utter_for_confirmation: utter_ask_replacement_confirmation
        utter_on_user_denial: utter_replacement_cancelled
      on_success: utter_replacement_disclaimer
      on_failure: utter_replacement_failed
```

- When `requires_confirmation:` is enabled, the prose must **not** also tell the
  model to ask the customer to confirm. Tell it to call the tool once the
  `requires:` inputs are present and let the engine ask. Doing both asks twice. The
  alternative is prose confirmation plus `requires:` on a confirmation memory key,
  without `requires_confirmation:`.
- Supplied confirmation response names must exist in `responses.yml` with a
  non-empty body. Unknown keys under a tool entry (a flat `ask_confirmation:`, for
  example) are rejected; use the nested `requires_confirmation`.
- If a supplied ask resolves to blank text after placeholder substitution, the call
  fails closed instead of pausing silently. A blank denial falls back to the model.
- When the user has to hear a specific fact, put the line in `responses.yml` and
  attach it with `on_success:` or `on_failure:`, rather than leaving the sentence to
  the model, which may summarize the result and drop the detail. `on_success`
  delivers the line and the turn goes on. When nothing may follow, deliver the line
  from an ordered block that ends with `action_listen`; that ends the turn without a
  model call, but a second question in the same user message goes unanswered.

Put `requires:` on every tool that places an order, a lock, or another side effect.
A gate is only as strong as the ways its fields can be written: list how each field
is set (`set_fields`, a `collect:` step, tool code, or a `set:` button) and close the
paths that should not open the gate. An `llm_settable` field can be set from a
remark before the question, which opens the gate early. When that is not
acceptable, reject the early write in a memory validation tool, or write the field
from tool code only.

## Conditions

Conditions appear in `requires:`, prose `if:`, ordered-block step `complete_when:`,
`utter:` `when:`, `next:` branches, and response variant `condition`. Every memory
reference has three segments: `session.<skill_id>.<entry>` for a skill's own memory,
`session.project.<entry>` for project memory. A bare key fails with
`Unknown name '<key>' in condition expression`.

- Truthiness: `session.card_replace.selected_card_id`
- Boolean combination: `session.card_replace.order_confirmed and
  session.card_replace.shipping_type`, `not session.card_replace.fraud_report_filed`
- Comparison: `session.card_replace.replacement_reason == 'stolen'`

A condition is a **string**; the map form (`selected_card_id: { exists: true }`) is
rejected. Use a folded `>` scalar in YAML when the expression spans lines.

## Skill-level `complete_when`

A **mapping** with `condition` (one condition string) and/or `criteria` (a list of
natural-language checks run when `complete` is called). A bare string is rejected.
It needs a skill with prose instructions; an ordered-block-only skill completes
through its block's `END`. With `criteria`, automatic completion is off and the
skill exits only through a successful `complete`. The check fails closed: if it
errors or times out, the skill stays open.

Write each `criteria` item as one check you can verify from the conversation (a
tool ran, a required question was asked). Prefer several short items to one long
sentence joined by "and" / "or", and put memory logic in `condition:`. Word each
item so a later turn cannot undo it: the check reads the whole conversation, so an
item that only matches the latest user message leaves the skill open after a
thank-you or a decline. Duplicate items are rejected. Ordered-block step
`complete_when:` stays a plain condition string.

The engine already tells the model when to call `complete()`: when the user is done
with the topic, and only after it has answered from relevant tool results. Leave
that guidance out of the body; it is sent on every active turn and can finish the
skill before a follow-up. Don't write "when the customer is satisfied, call
`@tool.complete`". Write a body sentence only when a step that looks finished is not
the real end (blocking a SIM does not finish the skill; it finishes after the
replacement is ordered or declined). `complete_when` is never shown to the model.

## Scoped instructions (`if:`)

Deterministic branching without restructuring. It pairs well with a `categorical`
memory entry; the framework strips non-matching paragraphs from the prompt once the
entry is set:

```markdown
if: session.card_replace.replacement_reason == 'stolen'
Tell the customer the card will be locked for their protection.
Confirm, then call @tool.lock_card.

if: session.card_replace.replacement_reason == 'lost' or session.card_replace.replacement_reason == 'not_received'
Call @tool.check_transactions and review recent transactions with them.
```

```yaml skills/card_replace/memory.yml
schema:
  public:
    replacement_reason:
      type: categorical
      enum_values: [lost, stolen, damaged, not_received]
      description: Why the card is being replaced.
```

- The condition is **the rest of that one line**. `if: >` followed by indented
  lines makes the condition the literal `>` and turns the condition text into the
  paragraph body. Keep it on one line, however long.
- One marker, `if:`. Write one paragraph per case, each with its own condition;
  `else:` in prose fails to compile. For exclusive either/or routing, use an
  ordered block's `next:` branches.
- A marker scopes only the paragraph right after it (up to the blank line).
  Unmarked paragraphs are always visible.

For an `llm_settable` field, a name and a type are not enough: the description
says which user answer sets it and which similar answers leave it unset. A
description is prose, not a control; when a wrong early write is costly, reject it
in a memory validation tool.

Continue from a choice the user already made when it is a preference: record it
with `@tool.set_fields` and carry on, asking only while the field is unset. Don't do
that for a field a `requires:` gate reads, because filling it from an earlier remark
opens the gate without the question it was meant to protect. When the action is
hard to undo, ask. A `collect:` step asks only while its field is unset, unless you
set `ask_before_filling`.

Tie a step to the fact that makes it true: place it under an `if:` on that fact,
not after a step the user might skip. To say a line the first time a fact is set,
use an `utter` trigger with `when:` (see `references/responses.md`).

## Memory in prose (`@memory`)

For a live memory value inside instructions the model reads (unmarked prose, text
under an `if:`, or ordered-block `instructions:`), use `@memory.project.<entry>` or
`@memory.<skill_id>.<entry>`. Readable memory while the skill is active: project
fields, other skills' **public** fields, and this skill's public and private fields.
Another skill's private fields and `@memory.system.*` fail validation.

At prompt build the engine substitutes the current value. An unset or unreadable
reference stays as the literal token. A set PII field becomes `[set]`.

```markdown
Use the already chosen card @memory.card_replace.selected_card_id for this request.
```

Keep `session.*` for structured YAML and conditions (`requires:`, `if:`,
`execute_tool` `parameters:`), and use `{session.*}` in `responses.yml`. A bare
`session.*` in free prose fails validation; so do incomplete tokens such as
`@memory.project`.
